subject: VastCorp MSA redlines — model output & training safeguards
messages:
From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@vastcorp.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: procurement@vastcorp.com, legal@vastcorp.com
Date: Thu, 2 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: VastCorp - MSA redlines: model output rights & data use

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the quick onboarding this week. Attached is our redline of the MSA — the two main open items for us are around (1) ownership/attribution for product outputs generated by the service, and (2) whether Redwood can use customer data or outputs to train or improve models (including any feedback/telemetry licenses).

High level asks from our side:
- We need clarity that VastCorp retains exclusive ownership of outputs produced by our internal prompts against our protected data.
- We want explicit opt-out language that prevents Redwood from using our raw content or outputs to train models that could be exposed to other customers.
- If Redwood wants to use any feedback/telemetry for product improvement, that must be aggregate and non-attributable to VastCorp and require a 30-day data retention maximum on raw logs.

Can you confirm whether Redwood has a standard clause we can propose, or if we need a separate addendum for training/feedback use? Attached: VastCorp_MSA_redlines.docx (tracked changes).

Would like to schedule a short sync with legal and product next week to resolve these points. Thanks — looking forward to your response.

Best,
Alice Chen
General Counsel, VastCorp

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.inference.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@vastcorp.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.inference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Thu, 2 May 2028 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VastCorp - MSA redlines: model output rights & data use

Alice — thanks for the redline and clear summary. I’ve looped in Karthik from Product (technical constraints) and Priya from Sales/Legal ops so we can provide a consolidated position.

Initial responses to your bullets:
- Output ownership: we generally grant customers a perpetual, worldwide, transferable right to use Outputs (the text/images/etc. generated from the Service). We do not claim ownership of customer outputs. However, we need reasonable rights to use Outputs and telemetry for service operation and aggregate product improvement.
- Training use: Redwood does not intend to provide customer-derived data or Outputs to third parties or sell customer models. We do have a product improvement pipeline that — by default — uses telemetry and de-identified samples to improve models. We can offer an explicit "training opt-out" for customers where Redwood will not use raw customer data or outputs to train models used by other customers, subject to operational constraints (e.g., latency on strict opt-outs for legacy data).
- Retention: 30-day retention on raw request bodies is operationally reasonable for Hosted customers; for Dedicated/Private deployments we can offer stricter controls.

Proposed next steps:
1) Karthik will propose contract language that balances (a) your request for a narrow opt-out and (b) our need to maintain a small window for telemetry/quality analysis.
2) I’ll schedule a 30-min call with VastCorp legal + product + Redwood product/legal to walk the redlines and proposed wording.
3) If the opt-out needs to be permanent, we’ll capture it in the Order Form (with potential pricing implication).

Can you share a few time slots Monday-Tuesday next week? I’ll prepare a short two-slide summary for the call.

—Mina
Mina Haddad
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.inference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Thu, 2 May 2028 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VastCorp - MSA redlines: model output rights & data use

Mina/Priya — quick technical summary and suggested clause language to consider adding to the redline.

Technical constraints:
- Our telemetry pipeline ingests request/response pairs and aggregated metrics; de-identification (hashing/pseudonymization) is automatic for hosted customers, but full removal requires a flagged opt-out and can take up to 72 hours to propagate through training datasets.
- For customers who require absolute non-use for training, we recommend Dedicated/Private deployment or a contract-level training opt-out tied to a higher monthly commitment to cover lost improvement signal.

Suggested clause (draft text you can paste into tracked changes):
"Redwood shall have no right to use Customer Data or Customer Outputs to train models that are served to third parties if Customer elects the Training Opt-Out in the Order Form. For Hosted Customers that do not elect the Training Opt-Out, Redwood may use de-identified and aggregated telemetry, logs, and Output snippets for the limited purpose of improving service reliability and model quality. Redwood will retain raw request and response data for no more than thirty (30) days unless otherwise required for security or legal investigation."

Notes:
- We should also add a short definition for "de-identified" to avoid ambiguity.
- If VastCorp needs the opt-out but still wants model improvements, propose a separate private model training offering where Redwood trains a customer-specific model on their data in an isolated bucket.

Happy to refine before we send to VastCorp.

—Karthik
Staff Product Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.inference.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@vastcorp.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.inference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference.com>, legal@vastcorp.com
Date: Fri, 3 May 2028 00:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VastCorp - MSA redlines: model output rights & data use

Alice — thanks again for the redline. We’ve reviewed internally and proposed specific language below (I’ve also attached a short redline summary). If any of this looks acceptable, we can incorporate the language into your tracked document and set a 30-minute legal sync.

Proposed language (one-paragraph summary for the MSA / Order Form):
1) Output ownership: Customer retains ownership of Customer Data and Customer Outputs. Redwood grants Customer a perpetual, non-exclusive license to use Outputs. Redwood will not assert ownership over Outputs.
2) Training & Feedback: Customer may elect a Training Opt-Out in the Order Form. If elected, Redwood will not use Customer Data or Customer Outputs to train models that are served to other customers. For Hosted Customers that do not elect the Opt-Out, Redwood may use de-identified and aggregated telemetry and Output excerpts solely for service improvement. Any use of Customer Data for improvement will exclude raw, identifiable content and will be subject to a thirty (30) day retention limit for raw request/response logs except when required for security or legal reasons.
3) Private training offering: If Customer requires model improvements on their data without sharing signals with others, Redwood can offer a private training engagement (billing and operational terms to be in the Order Form).

Next steps:
- I attached redline_summary_v1.xlsx with the clause text and rationale; I can paste track-changes into your document if you prefer.
- Proposed times for a legal/product sync: Mon 5/6 09:00-09:30 PT or Mon 5/6 16:00-16:30 PT. Please confirm which works.

If you need the opt-out reflected immediately, note that it’s typically captured in the Order Form (we’ll include pricing impact there).

Appreciate the fast turnaround — we want to make sure the final wording meets your compliance needs.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redline_summary_v1.xlsx

From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@vastcorp.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: procurement@vastcorp.com, legal@vastcorp.com, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Fri, 3 May 2028 02:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VastCorp - MSA redlines: model output rights & data use

Mina/Karthik — thanks for the clear proposal and the draft language. That addresses most of our concerns. Two quick clarifications before the sync:
- Can you add an explicit definition for "de-identified" (e.g., redaction of PII and removal of persistent identifiers such that outputs cannot be linked back to a specific VastCorp account)?
- We need to ensure that audit logs capturing who submitted a request are retained for at least 6 months for compliance (but we are OK if raw request bodies are only retained for 30 days). Can Redwood support 6-month retention for non-content metadata?

If you can add those two clarifications into the one-paragraph summary, we’ll accept the redline and confirm the 5/6 sync at 09:00 PT.

Thanks — Alice
Alice Chen
General Counsel, VastCorp
